purpose.turn_behavioral_observations_int: Turn behavioral observations into understandable audiences, then explore how those audiences could connect to customer reporting.
purpose.league_of_legends_is_an_online_g: League of Legends is an online game where people choose playable characters and can enter competitive matches. This project uses those observations as a practical case study in understanding users. You do not need game knowledge to follow the story.
purpose.riot_s_api_supplies_dated_charac: Riot's API supplies dated character activity and competitive records. These are the source observations behind the profiles.
purpose.models_turn_those_records_into_e: Models turn those records into estimates and audience descriptions. They help us compare groups; they do not explain why people behave differently.
purpose.generated_purchase_records_demon: Generated purchase records demonstrate customer reporting on real profiles. They do not reveal what these players actually buy.
purpose.introduce_activity_and_competiti: Introduce activity and competitive standing, one dimension at a time.
purpose.explore_character_interests_then: Explore character interests, then combine the dimensions into a useful audience profile.
purpose.carry_that_audience_into_the_sim: Carry that audience into the simulated purchase scenario, then inspect the engineering and evidence.
purpose.compact_repeated_observations_bu: Compact, repeated observations build useful profiles under a limited request allowance. Each analytical chapter starts with an overview. Use the question dropdown to explore each chapter. Combine brings the dimensions together; its selected question continues into Purchases.
purpose.how_the_evidence_reaches_this_st: How the evidence reaches this story
purpose.collection_dated_history_and_aud: Collection, dated history and audience models feed a checked local export. A separate generated-purchase branch demonstrates the commercial connection. Select a node to inspect its source or documentation.

interest.one_character_can_contribute_to: One character can contribute to several families
interest.every_member_clears_15k_in_this: Every member clears 15k in this example. Full active lifetime mastery is the denominator. Spread reflects overlapping scores, not six independent interests.

chapter.primer.accumulated_play_competit: Accumulated play, competitive frequency and retained history answer different questions. Competitive activity covers one participation channel; history is a lower bound from retained activity, not an account creation date.
chapter.primer.standing_is_a_position_on: Standing is a position on an ordered competitive ladder. The reference distribution explains how common each band is. Compare activity groups, or compare standing groups within a shared frequency band.
chapter.primer.characters_have_different: Characters have different play styles. Overlapping character families and eight player archetypes summarize interests. A player can express several archetypes. Names describe character styles, not skill or commercial value.
chapter.primer.construct_an_audience_by_: Construct an audience by combining the dimensions you have seen. Keep a shared context, define A and B, and check their support and overlap.
chapter.primer.these_audiences_are_linke: These audiences are linked to simulated purchase records. Ask who buys, how much buyers spend, how often they buy and whether their content purchases favor cosmetic items or playable-character unlocks.

charts.distribution.limited_support_requ: Limited support: requires 30 profiles and effective N 20.

charts.heatmap.joint_share_within_this_a: Joint share within this audience · fixed 0–100% color scale.
charts.heatmap.categories_stay_fixed_acr: {value} Categories stay fixed across audience selections. “limited” retains sparse mass; inspect cells for support.
scale.primary_interest_over_under_the_pa: Primary interest over / under the parent
scale.original_weights_denominator_score: Original weights; denominator: scored profiles including weak/tied matches.
charts.median.limited_scored_support_con: Limited scored support; conditions have not been widened.
charts.median.selected_primary_share_par: Selected primary share ÷ parent share − 1. Zero is parity; +50% is 1.5×. Parent zero is unavailable. This contextual ratio does not correct character popularity.
charts.distribution.identical_audiences_: Identical audiences provide no A/B contrast; inspect the parent-relative representation only if useful.
charts.distribution.primary_identity_is_: Primary identity is restricted by the definition; its representation is not a finding.
interests.companions.full_selected_audie: Full selected audience denominator. Describing interests requires at least four model-active characters. Unavailable interests do not imply no interests.
interests.no_additional_archetype_meets_: No additional archetype meets the expression threshold. Smaller strengths may still exist.
interests.companions.single_and_blend_pr: Single and Blend profiles remain in the denominator.
interests.companions.share_of_selected_s: Share of selected scored profiles with strength ≥0.20. {value} Shares can overlap; they are not normalized popularity.
interestOnly.observed_profiles_of_the_ad: {profiles} observed profiles · {value} of the adjusted base · effective N {effective_n}
why.a_customer_can_have_substantial_hist: A customer can have substantial historical use but low recent visit frequency. Volume, frequency and history answer different questions; competition here covers one participation channel.
why.audience_composition_can_change_a_po: Audience composition can change a pooled comparison. Standing supplies context; it is not a measure of customer worth.
why.in_retail_products_repeatedly_chosen: In retail, products repeatedly chosen by the same customers can form product groups, and customers’ mixes across them can describe interests. Here the observations are character usage, not shopping baskets or all market sales.
why.intersect_characteristics_to_define_: Intersect characteristics to define an audience for a product question, then check whether enough people remain to describe it.
why.buyer_participation_spending_per_buy: Buyer participation, spending per buyer and content mix support different product questions.
comparison.read_accumulated_play_and_com: Read accumulated play and competition together
comparison.distribution_within_this_stan: Distribution within this standing band; sparse mass retained.
interests.adcs_ranged_sustained_attacker: ADCs: ranged sustained attackers (attack damage carries).
interests.primary_match_selects_a_unique: Primary match selects a unique non-Diffuse strongest match. Expressed interest selects any chosen archetype with strength ≥0.20. Multiple archetypes use OR.
builder.select_any_number_of_segments_no: Select any number of segments. No selection means unrestricted, including unavailable values. Collapsing a section keeps its filters active.
builder.pending_edits_displayed_results_: Pending edits: displayed results still use the last applied definition.
builder.competitive_frequency_starter_un: Competitive frequency starter · unrestricted shared context
builder.values_within_a_field_use_or_dif: Values within a field use OR; different fields and shared conditions use AND. Changes apply together.
status.pending_edits_displayed_results_s: Pending edits: displayed results still use the last applied definition.
jointView.joint_distributions_within_eac: Joint distributions within each audience. This differs from the small maps’ original-base denominator.
metric.participation_includes_nonbuyers_: Participation includes nonbuyers. Cash per purchaser is USD in the 60-day window. Cosmetic items change appearance; character unlocks add playable characters. The percentage counts cosmetic purchases out of all cosmetic and character-unlock purchases across the audience, over all simulated history. It measures purchase events, rather than spending amounts.
simulation.how_this_purchase_scenario_wa: How this purchase scenario was built
simulation.the_scenario_combines_real_be: The scenario combines real behavioral profiles with explicitly designed spending assumptions and reproducible random variation. These shape purchase frequency, transaction activity and content choices so the complete customer-reporting workflow can be demonstrated and verified.
simulation.the_specialist_modifier_adds_: The specialist modifier adds 0.10 to the cosmetic-content generation control. Other offsets, bounds and randomness also apply; this is not a promise of a 10-point difference in the final reported cosmetic share.
simulation.generated_events_survive_iden: Generated events survive identity association, dated modeling and reconciliation. Recovering an imposed relationship demonstrates that reporting path. Assumptions were not calibrated to real customers.
simulation.cash_top_ups_count_as_cash_on: Cash top-ups count as cash once. Spending game currency on content is a separate event, not more cash revenue. The eight archetypes were attached later, not used as generator inputs.
families.evidence.all_173_characters_are: All 173 characters are covered in 25 overlapping families, with 251 memberships. Minimum family consistency is 94%. The accepted relative-Jaccard floor balances coverage, fit and family count.
families.evidence.the_review_floor_compa: The review floor compares a character's audience relationship with its own alternative-family reference. Stricter settings do not monotonically improve every measure. Twenty-four selected families use 20-repeat sources; one uses a 100-repeat source.
families.evidence.nmf_learned_eight_nonn: NMF learned eight nonnegative family profiles. Players can express mixtures; inference applies the same frozen profiles and training weights without refitting.
families.evidence.strongest_six_family_c: Strongest six family coordinates in the accepted unweighted-affinity profile scale; bars relative to this component's largest coordinate. These are strengths, not probabilities. No archetype-bootstrap stability is asserted. Names received informal player feedback.
families.evidence.the_toy_uses_cutoff_qu: The toy uses cutoff-qualified family affinities. The archetype input separately uses all model-active characters and lifetime weights without that cutoff.
families.evidence.weighted_audience_rela: Weighted audience relationships and strongest-neighbor graphs supported Leiden discovery. Full and anchored searches supplied candidates. Resampling and reviewed coverage/member-fit gates shaped the final overlapping families; this is not one automatic partition.
families.evidence.characters_repeatedly_: Characters repeatedly grouped together when source players were resampled. Overlap is intentional: {value} members also occur in another accepted family.
families.evidence.fit_of_each_member_rev: Fit of each member · review floor 80%
families.evidence.self_pairs_excluded_we: Self-pairs excluded. Weakest member: {value}. These saved diagnostics were reused in selection; they are not held-out accuracy or calibrated confidence. Matrix and fit come from this family's exact saved source, not pooled sources.
families.evidence.accepted_family_eviden: Accepted family evidence and selection limits
capabilities.full_page_discovery_uses_20: Full-page discovery uses 206 core calls for 205 players; ordinary known-player refresh uses two.
capabilities.at_discovery_and_follow_up_: At discovery and follow-up. Repeated compact observations trade match detail for broader history. These are conditional costs, not measured throughput.
capabilities.partial_work_needs_an_expla: Partial work needs an explanation before retry or cleanup.
capabilities.sqlite_links_source_tasks_t: SQLite links source tasks to files, compaction and load state.
capabilities.at_integrity_gates_and_diag: At integrity gates and diagnosis. This is task/file lineage, not automated column lineage.
capabilities.reapplying_a_dated_observat: Reapplying a dated observation must not reapply its refresh effects.
capabilities.postgresql_upserts_require_: PostgreSQL upserts require a newer observation timestamp; repeated/older observations are ignored.
capabilities.after_confirmed_ingestion_a: After confirmed ingestion and during state-update retries. This scoped idempotency does not imply end-to-end exactly-once delivery.
capabilities.competing_claimants_need_di: Competing claimants need distinct work and recoverable ownership.
capabilities.postgresql_row_locks_skip_l: PostgreSQL row locks, SKIP LOCKED and claim tokens reserve work; expiry and renewal handle stale owners.
capabilities.during_discovery_and_refres: During discovery and refresh. Atomicity is within the database transaction; a multi-machine deployment has not been demonstrated.
capabilities.concurrent_calls_can_otherw: Concurrent calls can otherwise overspend a shared client allowance.
capabilities.locks_and_a_token_bucket_co: Locks and a token bucket coordinate requests within one client.
capabilities.during_api_calls_shared_cla: During API calls. Shared claims do not globally throttle separate clients. Current evidence does not establish an actively multithreaded production runner.
capabilities.an_upload_can_succeed_while: An upload can succeed while ingestion or modeling fails.
capabilities.wait_for_confirmed_ingestio: Wait for confirmed ingestion before dependent completion updates; run dbt separately and preserve inputs if a later stage fails.
capabilities.at_every_delivery_cycle_ser: At every delivery cycle. Service boundaries are not one distributed transaction; injected live recovery remains untested.
capabilities.stage_outcomes_must_explain: Stage outcomes must explain both success and partial work.
capabilities.console_events_job_results_: Console events, job results, integrity reports and the ledger retain different parts of the execution story.
capabilities.during_operation_and_review: During operation and review. Fixed report paths can be overwritten; archive matching records by run.
capabilities.reviewers_need_a_usable_res: Reviewers need a usable result without warehouse credentials.
capabilities.versioned_models_an_explici: Versioned models, an explicit manifest and checked local Parquets feed the viewer.
capabilities.at_export_and_viewing_refre: At export and viewing. Refresh is manual and snapshot dates remain visible.

render.three_dimensions_of_activity_thre: Three dimensions of activity. Three different questions.
render.how_much_accumulated_play_how_oft: How much accumulated play, how often competitively, and how far back does the retained activity reach?
render.estimated_hours_lifetime_mastery_: Estimated hours = lifetime mastery points / 1,200, assuming 600 points and 30 minutes per match. Frequency is recorded competitive wins + losses under a one-year-season assumption. History is a minimum known span from retained last-play timestamps. Terminology changes labels, not membership.
render.next_competitive_standing_adds_po: Next: competitive standing adds position to participation.
render.compare_positions_on_the_ladder_w: Compare positions on the ladder without replacing the activity dimensions.
render.what_people_choose_adds_another_d: What people choose adds another dimension.
render.which_interest_patterns_accompany: Which interest patterns accompany different behavioral profiles?
render.understand_the_archetype_names_an: Understand the archetype names and mixtures
render.adcs_means_ranged_sustained_attac: ADCs means ranged sustained attackers (attack damage carries). Bruisers/Tanks are durable close-range characters; Mages/Enchanters use spells or strengthen allies; Assassins/Duelists favor focused attacks; Front-Line Disablers interrupt; Control Mages restrict space; Burst Mages concentrate damage; Aggressive Junglers initiate pressure from between lanes.
render.single_one_strength_meets_0_20_bl: Single: one strength meets 0.20. Blend: several meet it. Diffuse: none does. A unique non-Diffuse primary supports primary-interest comparisons; naming feedback is not statistical validation.
render.choose_a_question_above_primary_i: Choose a question above. Primary-interest comparisons cover all profiles with a unique non-Diffuse primary, without preset activity restrictions.
render.construct_an_audience_around_your: Construct an audience around your question.
render.edit_the_shared_context_and_indep: Edit the shared context and independent A/B conditions, then apply them together.

render.next_opens_purchases_using_the_la: Next opens Purchases using the last applied definition. Pending edits are not carried.
